newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end lower-limit down, hogs tumble.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end lower-limit down, hogs tumble.

text.p: February CME pork belly futures fell for a limit loss for the second consecutive day on delivery concerns while hog futures finished sharply lower on weak cash hog prices. Technicals also pressured markets, traders said.

Pork bellies ended down the 3.000-cent-a-lb limit to down 2.050 cent with February limit down at 73.175 cents and March down 2.200 at 73.375 cents. Hog futures finished 1.125 to 0.150 cent a lb lower with April off most at 72.075 cents.
Pork bellies sank on carryover selling from last Friday's limit losses in March and May with continued pressure reflecting delivery concerns, traders said.

No strong stopper developed for February deliveries and locals liquidated February positions into sell stops. Back months followed on stops and technical pressure before late short covering surfaced, they said.
"The wrong guys are taking deliveries -- it makes the whole market bearish," a belly trader said.
Adding to overall weakness was the recent decline in cash bellies. Prices for cash bellies slipped to four-month lows despite a recent reduction in slaughter, traders noted.
"It all relates back to demand. Without the fast food chains coming to the rescue I think this (cash) market will continue to work lower," said Dan Vaught, livestock analyst for AG Edwards.
Another problem that has been weighing on pork bellies and hogs has been a slowdown in pork exports, traders said.
"Pork exports are down because of the value of the dollar," said Rich Tokheim at Investment Research Co.
The weakness in pork and expected continued slow packer demand added to technical pressure in hogs, traders said.
Cash hogs have eased to lowest prices in four months following a recent setback in cash pork values. This has left most futures contracts at a premium, they said.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.08 at $73.30 per cwt and June hog futures closed at 77.450 cents.
Adding to losses was a weak technical picture. April filled the gap left in charts after the last USDA Hogs and Pigs report and June was closing that gap, they added.
General wire house selling and closing sell stops kept April at day's lows late. Only Rand Financials was cited as a light buyer, pit sources said.
